messages.subject: Home range along road corridors
parts:
Hi ctmm users,

I have been working on home range estimation of a bunch of marsupials'. They are using the linear habitat along the road corridor amidst the paddocks. But their estimated range is spilling across their used space with unsuitable habitat. I came across this communication, and revised my script:

# Defining function
is_inaccessible <- function(x, y) {
  return(x < min(x) || x > max(x) && y < min(y) || y > max(y))
  return(TRUE)
}

# Running models

FITS <- UDS <- Occur <- list()

for(i in 1:length(dat_onlyTwo))
{
  print(i)
  GUESS <- ctmm.guess(data[[i]],interactive=FALSE)
  FITS[[i]] <- ctmm.select(data[[i]],GUESS,trace=2)
  UDS[[i]] <- akde(data[[i]],FITS[[i]])
 
  for (row in 1:nrow(UDS[[i]]$CDF)) {
    for (col in 1:ncol(UDS[[i]]$CDF)) {
      if (is_inaccessible(UDS[[i]]$r$x[row], UDS[[i]]$r$y[col])) {
        UDS[[i]]$CDF[row, col] <- 1
      }
    }
  }
 
  Occur[[i]] <- occurrence(data[[i]],FITS[[i]])
}

Unfortunately, this is not working. I would appreciate any input at this point.

Thanks in advance!

Damber

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Home range along road corridors
parts:
Hi Damber,

You do not need to do this by hand any more. There is a better method that is implemented in akde(), which can now take an SP argument for the boundary and it will make the adjustment at the kernel level. A paper is coming out on this soon.
https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/reference/akde.html

Also, if they have strong selection to a covariate that you know, then you can improve that even further with RSF-AKDEs.

Best,
Chris
